docs.title: Autonomous Potential Violation Eradicator (APVE)
docs.text:
Author: blackgeyer (Also known as blackgaier) | Version: 1.3.5 | License: GPLv3

APVE is an ultra-fast, high-performance chat filter plugin designed to keep chat free from profanity, advertisements, adult content, and other potentially malicious material.

It uses the Aho-Corasick algorithm combined with fuzzy matching for high efficiency, even on high-traffic chats. Powered by PacketEvents for minimal server load, unlike the standard Bukkit API.

APVE officially supports only English and Russian languages, as other languages are problematic to normalize and check for violations.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
All of them will send messages.perm-fail to player if he has no permission to execute this command.

Command Description Permission Default /apve General command. Will display help text if it has been written without any argument. apve.use OP /apve reload Reloads the APVE. apve.reload OP /apve warns show {player-nickname} Displays the number of warnings and the most serious types of violations in recent times. apve.warns.show OP /apve warns remove {player-nickname} {integer} Clears a specified number of warnings for the player. The number of warnings to be cleared is equal to the integer argument. apve.warns.remove OP /apve warns clear {player-nickname} Clears all warnings for the player. apve.warns.clear OP /apve help Displays help text. apve.help OP /apve notify toggle Toggles the notifies about violations. apve.notify.toggle OP /apve check {String} Checks the string for any violations. See details below. apve.check OP

docs.title: /apve check output details
docs.text:
After the check, displays the following information:

  • Input text — identical to the written {String}
  • Normalized text
  • Status — NONE, SUSPICIOUS or MALICIOUS

If status is MALICIOUS or SUSPICIOUS:

  • Found word
  • Dictionary sample
  • Check details (violation type and information about which method was used to find it)

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Permission Description Default apve.violation.notify Allows receiving real-time chat notifications about player violations. False apve.insult.immune Grants immunity against general insult detections. False apve.fam.insult.immune Grants immunity against family insult detections. False apve.caps.immune Grants immunity against upper-case (caps) filter. False apve.spam.immune Grants immunity against spam filter. False apve.adult.content.immune Grants immunity against adult content filter. False apve.social.immune Grants immunity against social media links filter. False apve.advertisement.immune Grants immunity against advertisement and external resource sharing. False apve.staff.insult.immune Grants immunity against staff insult detections. False

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
After running APVE for the first time, a default configuration will be generated in the plugins/APVE directory, and APVE will apply the messages localization according to your system's current localization.

APVE will apply the correct syntax of the punishment command in the configuration if you have installed LibertyBans, AdvancedBans or LiteBans. Otherwise, you need to write the syntax manually based on your installed punishment plugin.

docs.title: Thresholds and language
docs.text:
Word similarity thresholds relative to any prohibited word. If a word's similarity does not exceed any threshold below, APVE will pass it. If a word's similarity equals or exceeds the medium threshold, APVE marks the word as SUSPICIOUS but will pass it. If a word's similarity equals or exceeds the high threshold, APVE marks the word as MALICIOUS. Some benign words may be similar to malicious ones. Consequently, a high threshold between 0.75 and 0.80 is strongly recommended to avoid false positives while still catching potentially malicious words. A medium threshold between 0.55 and 0.60 is strongly recommended to avoid passing specific or typo-entered malicious words.

Language is responsible for APVE's messages localization. Available values: ru, en and auto. If auto, APVE will apply messages localization according to your system's current localization. APVE will apply en_US.yml localization if your system's localization does not match any of the available localizations.

language: auto

thresholds:
  high: 0.78 
  medium: 0.57

docs.title: Dictionaries
docs.text:
Before writing words to the dictionaries, ensure you meet the following prerequisites: It should be written only using transliteration and the Latin alphabet (example: мразь ——> mrazb), without any symbols, numbers or spaces, in lowercase and phrased accounting for the normalizer's work. Beware of adding slang and short words to the dictionaries, as this may cause false positives. You can see information about normalizer work below.

insult-words:
- eblan
- mrazb
- dolboeb
# ...

docs.title: Family
docs.text:
Family pronouns. If APVE detects a message that contains a family pronoun alongside an insult word, it will detect it as FAMILY_INSULT.

family-insult-words:
- father
- mother
- matb
# ...

If APVE detects a word that has any of the inappropriate roots below, it detects it as a violation corresponding to the root's context.

family-roots:
- roditel
- opek
- mother
# ...

bad-roots:
- eblan
- dolboeb
- huesos
# ...

docs.title: Expressive Words
docs.text:
Responsible for allowing players to express their emotions with the words below. If a word's similarity is higher than any threshold but it is identical to an expressive word, APVE will pass it.

expressive-words:
- pizda
- pizdec
- blyatb
# ...

docs.title: Advertisement
docs.text:
APVE detects a message as advertisement if it has any ad-words below alongside a domain. You should write only the advertising resource, not the IP. (Example: 2b2t instead of 2b2t.org.) Words to ad-words can be written with numbers.

ad-words:
- 10b10t
- 123c
- 1f2d
# ...

docs.title: Social distribution
docs.text:
APVE will detect a message as SOCIAL_DIST if it has a social word alongside a domain. You should write social words the same way as ad words — no IP, only the advertising resource.

social:
- discord
- telegram
- tg
# ...

docs.title: Allowed words
docs.text:
Responsible for avoiding false positives if a benign word has an inappropriate root or resembles a prohibited word. APVE will pass a word if it is identical to any of the allowed-words.

allowed-words:
- corn
- mazb
- scunthorpe
# ...

adult-words:
- pornhub
- anasha
- methemfethamin
# ...

adult-roots:
- porn
- geroin
- intim
# ...

docs.title: Staff insults
docs.text:
APVE will detect a message as STAFF_INSULT if it contains a staff title alongside any insult word.

staff-tituls:
- admin
- helper
- sozdatel
# ...

docs.title: Punishments
docs.text: All parameters responsible for applying actions (punishments) to violators.

docs.title: Action command syntax
docs.text:
Commands that are dispatched according to the selected action in violation blocks. Must be configured for your punishment plugin's command syntax.

The command's arguments must be in the following order: * "command" %player% %duration% %reason%

Otherwise, the plugin will not apply the action correctly.

punishments:
  mute-command: mute %player% %duration% %reason%
  ban-command: ban %player% %duration% %reason%
  banip-command: banip %ip% %duration% %reason%
  kick-command: kick %player% %reason%

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
If punishments-is-enabled is false, APVE will not apply any action to the violator, regardless of warnings etc.

If auto-detect-plugin is true, APVE will automatically set the command syntax based on the installed punishment plugin. APVE can automatically set the command syntax only for LibertyBans, AdvancedBans and LiteBans. Otherwise, you will need to configure the command syntax manually.

auto-detect-plugin: true
punishments-is-enabled: true

perm-keywords:
- permanent
- perm
- infinity
- inf
- '-1'

Responsible for setting violation severity levels. The larger the integer, the more severe the violation. Based on this, APVE will punish the violator for the most severe of all committed violations.

priority:
  caps: 1
  spam: 2
  insult: 3
  adult-content: 4
  family-insult: 5
  staff-insult: 6
  soc-media-dist: 7
  ad-dist: 8

docs.title: Notifying parameters
docs.text:
If true, the plugin will not apply any action or warn to the violators. The plugin will only log every violation. This mode is incompatible with punishments and warns. Consequently, if you enable this mode alongside other actions, APVE's work will be aborted or limited.

audit-mode: false

If false, APVE will not send messages about player violations to the console.

console-log: false

If true, APVE will send notifications about violations in-game to players who have the apve.violation.notify permission.

notifies: true

docs.title: Action blocks
docs.text:
Each violation type has its own configuration block. The common parameters are:

  • is-enabled — whether this violation type is detected at all.
  • punishment-is-enabled — whether to apply a punishment upon violation. Requires punishments-is-enabled: true in the punishments block.
  • duration — punishment duration. Supports time units: s (seconds), m (minutes), h (hours), d (days).
  • type — punishment type: mute, ban, banip or kick.
  • blocking — if true, APVE will block the violating message from being delivered to chat.
  • censor — if true, APVE will replace the violating word with asterisks instead of blocking the entire message. Not applicable when blocking is true.

docs.title: Warn block
docs.text:
Controls the warning system. Warns are issued to the violator before a punishment is applied, if warns-is-enabled is true.

  • warn-limit — the number of warns after which the punishment is applied.
  • warn-limit-is-enabled — whether to apply a punishment upon reaching the warn limit.
  • warn_reset_when_server_restarts — if true, warns are reset on server restart.
  • temporary-warns — if true, warns expire after the period defined by warn-reset-time.
  • warn-reset-time — time after which warns are reset (e.g. 1h).
  • warn_reset_count — number of warns removed when the reset timer expires.
  • warns-is-enabled — whether the warn system is enabled at all.
warns:
  warn-limit: 2
  warn-limit-is-enabled: true

  warn_reset_when_server_restarts: true
  temporary-warns: true
  warn-reset-time: 1h
  warn_reset_count: 2
  warns-is-enabled: true

docs.title: Violation blocks
docs.text:
insult:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: true
  duration: 30m
  type: mute
  blocking: true
  censor: false

family-insult:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: true
  duration: 8h
  type: mute
  blocking: true
  censor: false

ad-dist:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: true
  duration: 30d
  type: banip
  blocking: true
  censor: false

soc-media-dist:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: true
  duration: 180m
  type: ban
  blocking: true
  censor: false

adult-content:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: true
  type: mute
  duration: 8h
  blocking: true
  censor: false

staff-insult:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: true
  type: mute
  duration: 12h
  blocking: true
  censor: false

docs.title: Spam block
docs.text:
The spam block has additional parameters:

  • max-similar-messages — maximum number of similar messages a player can send within a time window before the violation is triggered.
  • time-window-seconds — the time window in seconds during which similar messages are counted.
  • similarity-threshold — minimum similarity ratio for two messages to be considered duplicates. Range: 0.0–1.0.
spam:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: true
  max-similar-messages: 3
  time-window-seconds: 60
  similarity-threshold: 0.9
  type: mute
  duration: 20m
  blocking: false

docs.title: Caps block
docs.text:
The caps block has additional parameters:

  • min-message-length — minimum message length in characters required for the caps check to apply. Shorter messages are ignored.
  • min-caps-percentage — minimum percentage of uppercase characters required to trigger the violation.
caps:
  is-enabled: true
  punishment-is-enabled: false
  min-message-length: 6
  min-caps-percentage: 70
  type: mute
  duration: 15m
  blocking: false
  censor: false

docs.title: Intercepted commands
docs.text:
A list of commands whose arguments will be scanned for violations the same way as regular chat messages. Useful for covering private messaging commands so violations are not bypassed via /msg or similar.

intercepted-commands:
- msg
- w
- tell
# ...

docs.title: Blocked domains
docs.text:
A list of domain suffixes that APVE looks for when detecting advertisement and social distribution violations. Due to the text normalization process, domains like .gg must be written with a single character (e.g. g, not gg). Write all domains without dots.

blocked-domains:
- ru
- com
- net
# ...

docs.title: /apve check
docs.text:
The command-msg.check block configures the colors used in the output of the /apve check command, which displays the analysis result for a given player message.

  • malicious — color code applied to words classified as MALICIOUS.
  • suspicious — color code applied to words classified as SUSPICIOUS.
  • none — color code applied to words that passed the check with no flags.
command-msg:
  check:
    status-colors:
      malicious: '&c'
      suspicious: '&e'
      none: '&a'

docs.title: Around July 24 - 28, 2026
docs.text:
Around July 24, 2026, the development of APVE began. Back then, APVE had a different name — Autonomous Potential Toxicity Eradicator (APTE). Development went slowly because, alongside it, I was working on other projects like auction and economy plugins meant for an unpopular, still-unformed server — PoliticXServer (the server's name might have changed since then). It was during this timeframe that the initial architecture was laid out: intercepting messages at the network level instead of using AsyncPlayerChatEvent for the sake of better performance, the idea of a monolithic configuration, and minimizing hardcode as much as possible by adding the ability to freely change dictionaries and messages. Also, around July 28, the decision was made to use Aho-Corasick over other solutions in favor of even greater performance.

I was motivated by the fact that my creation would eventually be used on PoliticXServer, so I kept pushing APTE forward after finishing the other projects. To maintain the ability for APTE to work correctly and efficiently for both Russian and English audiences, the decision was made to force the TextNormalizer to convert all non-Latin characters into Latin, and force administrators to write words in the dictionaries using transliteration.

docs.title: July 30 - August 9, 2026
docs.text:
From July 30 to August 5, I was out of town, so development was temporarily paused. After returning home, I continued developing APTE, fixing bugs, adding new filters, etc. My development at that time was hindered by bad habits from my other projects—namely, NOT using Gradle, Git, and Maven, which significantly impacted the speed of testing and compiling.

On August 9, I decided to finally drop direct compilation via javac -cp and switch to compiling through Gradle, which led to an increase in the speed of development, testing, and maintenance efficiency. Due to the expansion of APTE's functionality, I thought that "Autonomous Potential Toxicity Eradicator" implied it only intercepted toxicity in the chat, so APTE was renamed to a more meaningful name — Autonomous Potential Violation Eradicator, which says that it intercepts the majority of chat violations.

docs.title: August 14 - 16, 2026
docs.text: On August 14, Git was initialized in the project folder. On August 16, the development of the first version of APVE was finished — APVE v1.0.0. At the time, this version was only published on SpigotMC and Modrinth, and was also sent to the owner of PoliticXServer. The GitHub repository was created later, on August 17, after I figured out the GitHub interface.

docs.title: August 17 - 19, 2026
docs.text:
On August 17, alongside the creation of the repository, the second version of APVE was released — APVE v1.1.0, which added the FoolProof system to find configuration errors upon startup, and the /apve reload command (yeah, APVE v1.0.0 was so raw that it didn't even include a basic /apve reload) so the plugin could be reloaded without needing to type /stop.

On August 18, another version came out — APVE v1.2.0, which only added the /apve warns show, /apve warns remove, and /apve warns clear commands to make testing and administration easier.

On August 19, APVE v1.2.2 was released, which included improvements to the FoolProof system and the ability to issue permanent punishments. The price of this addition was the partial loss of support for specific punishment plugins, because the ability to issue permanent punishments relied on substituting the duration argument with words like perm, -1, inf, and others, letting the punishment plugin know the time should be forever. Because of this, plugins that don't support this substitution couldn't issue the punishment correctly. Also, after this update, APVE could no longer correctly use command syntaxes where the arguments were NOT ordered exactly as %player% %duration% %reason%.

Also on August 19, I tried to upload the update to SpigotMC, but it just wouldn't upload. Because I forgot how to post an update on SpigotMC, I started clicking all the buttons to no avail. Eventually, out of anger, I abandoned my APVE SpigotMC page and put all my focus on Modrinth, BuiltByBit, and Hangar, where updates are published normally.

docs.title: August 21 - Late August, 2026
docs.text:
On August 21, APVE v1.2.5 was released, becoming the first stable release after the previous beta versions. In v1.2.5, the FoolProof system and the logging system were improved again, and an audit-mode was added to improve administration and support.

Closer to the end of August, a conflict occurred between me and the owners of PoliticXServer. The owners were dumping heavy tasks solely on me and one of the idea guys, completely ignoring the fact that others either had no tasks or weren't doing them. The relationship between me and the owners was already tense lately, but the final requests—"Florian, go write a Towny addon" and "you and the idea guy come up with server rules and mechanics"—became the last straw. I cut off all communication with the owners as well as the participants in creating PoliticXServer. I don't regret this decision one bit, even if it hurt some of the participants. I got more time to support and promote APVE, and I became independent of anyone else.

docs.title: August 23 - 26, 2026
docs.text:
On August 23, a minor APVE update was released — APVE v1.2.51, which improved the configuration error detection implemented by FoolProof, and also improved the default config.yml for a better Out-of-the-Box experience.

On August 24, APVE v1.2.6 was released, which fixed an NCI bypass where a player could type b a d w o r d or ba d wor d and not get punished. After this update, APVE got one step closer to the status of being one of the best chat filtering plugins.

On August 26, APVE v1.3.0 was released, adding a player violation notification system, a new punishment block filter — STAFF_INSULT, and permissions to bypass punishments.

docs.title: August 26 - September 5, 2026
docs.text:
From August 26 to September 5, I decided to take a break from development and make a YouTube video about APVE's effectiveness to promote the plugin. However, during filming, a few critical bugs were found that I had introduced in the v1.3.0 update.

On September 5, I released APVE v1.3.1, which fixed a critical bug with FAMILY_INSULT detection. Previously, the plugin punished for simply mentioning a pronoun found in family-insult-word/family-roots. Now, it allows the mention of pronouns, but if it finds insult-words/bad-words next to it, APVE perceives it as a FAMILY_INSULT, which makes sense. Also, the v1.3.1 update added the /apve check {String} command to quickly check inputs for violations directly through the console where the server's Java process is running.

docs.title: September 5 - 22, 2026
docs.text:
From September 5 to September 22, I decided to take another break from development and, alongside it, shoot a couple of YouTube videos about APVE and try to advertise it on other social networks. I ran into problems with the latter: regular admins didn't want to configure the settings, which was one of the most crucial steps after installation for APVE to work correctly.

That's when I made the decision to radically improve the Out-Of-The-Box experience by adding automatic localization application based on the system's locale, adding 1,456 server names to the ad-words dictionary in the default config, switching to miniMessage, and auto-applying command syntax depending on the installed punishment plugin. All of the above was added in the new v1.3.5 update that came out on September 22.

docs.title: About Installation
docs.text: Follow these steps to install APVE on your server:

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Before installation, ensure your server environment meets the following prerequisites:

  • Server Core: Installed Server Core must be Bukkit-Based like Paper, Spigot, Purpur etc and it must be designed to minecraft version newer or equal to 1.20.6. Note: APVE doesn't tested on 26.3 version. Consequently, proper plugin operation on this version or higher is not guaranteed.
  • Java Version: Java 21 or higher.
  • Dependencies: PacketEvents (Spigot version) and Adventure API if your server core doens't have Adventure API included natively. (Like Spigot)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download the plugin: Download the latest .jar release of APVE from Modrinth / Hangar / SpigotMC / BuildByBit / Github Repository Beware from unofficial websites!

  2. Install Dependencies: Ensure PacketEvents is placed inside your server's /plugins/ directory.

  3. Add APVE: Place the downloaded apve.jar file into the /plugins/ directory.

  4. Start or Reload the server: Start or restart your server to generate the default configuration files. ```bash # Do not use /reload — this may cause undefined behavior. Full server restart is recommended.

docs.title: Normalizer Work
docs.text:
Before every word check for violation, APVE normalizes it with TextNormalizer class to avoid filter bypasses like b-a-d-w-o-r-d or mрA3b.

TextNormalizer clears message from every Unicode, diacritical marks, minecraft colors (like &a), symbols, numbers. It translates homoglyphs and leet speak to their latinic identical (Or to their similar). It also removes repeated letters that appear consecutively. (e.g. baaaaaad wooooord —> bad word, insignificant fuuck —> insignificant fuck)

Additionally, it transliterates all non-Latin characters into the Latin alphabet. If a character lacks a direct Latin equivalent, the closest matching letter combination is used.

All words to dictionaries should be writted only in translit with latinic alphabet, without any symbol, number, space or uppercase letter.

Below has been showed the human readable TextNormalizer normalizing table:

    Transliteration

    а —> a       б —> b       в —> v       г —> g
    д —> d       е —> e       ё —> e       ж —> zh
    з —> z       и —> i       й —> y       к —> k
    л —> l       м —> m       н —> n       о —> o
    п —> p       р —> r       с —> s       т —> t
    у —> u       ф —> f       х —> h       ц —> c
    ч —> ch      ш —> sh      щ —> sch     ъ —> empty
    ы —> y       ь —> b       э —> e       ю —> yu
    я —> ya      

    Diacritical Transliteration
    α —> a       β —> b       γ —> g
    δ —> d       ε —> e       η —> n       θ —> th
    ι —> i       κ —> k       λ —> l       μ —> m
    ν —> v       ο —> o       π —> p       ρ —> r
    σ —> s       τ —> t       υ —> u       χ —> x
    ψ —> ps      ω —> w       ø —> o       ð —> d
    þ —> th      æ —> ae      œ —> oe      ŋ —> n
    ß —> s       ł —> l       đ —> d       ħ —> h
    ĸ —> k       ı —> i       

    Leet Speak convertion
    0 —> o       1 —> i
    3 —> z       4 —> ch      5 —> s       6 —> b
    8 —> b       @ —> a       $ —> s       ! —> i
    | —> i       + —> t       € —> e       £ —> l
    ¥ —> y       

    Symbol cleaning
    § —> empty   * —> empty   _ —> empty
    - —> empty   . —> empty   , —> empty   / —> empty
    \ —> empty   ~ —> empty   ` —> empty   ' —> empty
    " —> empty   = —> empty   ^ —> empty   # —> empty
    & —> empty   ( —> empty   ) —> empty   [ —> empty
    ] —> empty   { —> empty   } —> empty

    Patterns

    (?i)[&§]([0-9a-fk-or]|#[0-9a-f]{6}|x([&§][0-9a-f]){6})") Clears every minecraft legacy color 

    [\\p{Cf}\\p{Cc}\\u200B-\\u200D\\uFEFF\\u00AD] Clears every invisible chars

    ("\\p{M}") Clears combining marks (Diacritical)
